messages:
acme_ops: Hey team, streaming inference to our Private deployment started failing after we rolled a new corporate FW policy. Clients get repeated HTTP/2 stream resets and gRPC errors (UNAVAILABLE / code=14). We only see this when traffic goes via corp-proxy; direct traffic from a bastion works. Can you advise?

julie_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact client error and the target host:port you call?

acme_ops: Error from our app: `rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed with unknown error` logs show `RST_STREAM` and `HTTP/2: PROTOCOL_ERROR`. Target is `inference.private.redwood.internal:9412` (gRPC streaming).

sam_sre: Two quick hypotheses: 1) TLS inspection / proxy removing ALPN/h2 so HTTP/2 negotiation fails. 2) Firewall/NAT altering TCP MSS / causing TLS record fragmentation on port 9412. Can you run an openssl client test from a host that goes through the proxy? e.g. `openssl s_client -connect inference.private.redwood.internal:9412 -alpn h2 -servername inference.private.redwood.internal`

acme_ops: Ran that from a client that goes through corp-proxy. Output excerpt: ```ALPN protocol: (NONE)``` No h2. Also the proxy stack shows TLS inspection enabled and a rewrite cert.

matt_eng: That ALPN result is the smoking gun. gRPC requires ALPN=h2 for HTTP/2 over TLS. If the proxy terminates TLS and re-terminates without advertising `h2` ALPN, the client and server never negotiate HTTP/2 and the gRPC layer will fall back/timeout and produce stream resets.

julie_support: Actions we recommend: 1) Configure the corporate TLS proxy/firewall to preserve/pass ALPN including `h2`, or 2) Bypass TLS inspection for traffic to the inference hostname (add to allowlist), or 3) Use our HTTPS REST gateway on standard ports (443) while you get proxy updated.

sam_sre: Also check that the proxy isn't downgrading TLS versions or stripping necessary ciphers. Quick debug commands: `curl --http2 -v https://inference.private.redwood.internal:9412/health` and `openssl s_client -alpn h2 -connect inference.private.redwood.internal:9412 -servername inference.private.redwood.internal -showcerts` — compare outputs from behind the proxy and from a bastion that bypasses it.

acme_ops: Ran the curl test: behind proxy `* Using HTTP/1.1` and `HTTP/1.1 400`, from bastion `* Using HTTP/2` and `HTTP/2 200`. We'll ask SecOps to exempt `inference.private.redwood.internal:9412` from TLS inspection.

matt_eng: If SecOps is resistant to exempting hostnames, they can also configure the proxy to advertise `h2` and allow TLS passthrough for that SNI. Note: some enterprise proxies only support ALPN advertise for 443; if that's the case mapping 9412 -> 443 for egress or using the REST fallback is quickest.

julie_support: For completeness — please also verify outbound NACL/SG rules: ensure egress to Redwood IP ranges is allowed on TCP/9412 and return traffic ephemeral ports (1024-65535) are open for the NAT gateway. A stateless NACL deny on return ephemeral ports can produce similar ambiguous resets.

acme_ops: SecOps updated the proxy: enabled ALPN passthrough for that SNI and added the host to the TLS inspect bypass list. After that our gRPC streams are stable. Thanks! :tada:

deploy-bot: Incident #SUP-2026-0423 created for tracking (assigned -> sam_sre).

julie_support: Great — marking this as resolved on our side. If you want a permanent option, we can coordinate with your SecOps to publish the required egress entries (hostnames + IP prefixes) and a short ALPN compatibility note for their firewall vendor.

acme_ops: Please do. We'll take the recommended egress list and the ALPN note. Thanks everyone.
